A LITTLE MORE ABOUT ME

Connecting dots.
Building forward.

I’m Abhishek, a builder working across healthcare AI, product strategy and founder’s office operations. Mechanical engineering taught me to think in systems; my M.Tech in Techno-Entrepreneurship at IIT Hyderabad taught me to test whether those systems solve a problem people care about.

The journey so far.

I care about what a result actually tells us. Interviews validate a problem; a prototype tests an idea; a pilot tests a workflow. Sustained adoption and revenue need their own evidence. This distinction guides how I build, measure and change direction.

2024 — PRESENT

Founder · Healthcare AI Product

Aivana Health Intelligence

Started venture development in 2024 and formally registered the company in 2025. Conducted 370+ structured interviews over 18 months with medical students, clinicians and hospital administrators.

Built Kaya, an AI clinical-reasoning simulator, then redirected the product through decision support to documentation automation as field evidence changed the priorities. Designed an 11-week, 371-consultation hospital pilot with physician review.

Researched 12 clinical AI vendors and created five institutional workflow demonstrations to support partner conversations.

MARCH — AUGUST 2026

Founder’s Office Associate · Growth & Operations

Dyadic Health

Designed a shared CRM, KPI dashboards and SOPs for partner onboarding, customer coordination and launch execution. Reported founder review time fell from roughly four hours to 50 minutes per day.

Coordinated onboarding and operational readiness for 11 healthcare and eldercare partners. Built a 200+ member caregiver community, generated 35 discovery conversations and coordinated the first paid caregiver cohort’s launch.

FEBRUARY — AUGUST 2025

Co-Founder & COO

GnixarAcademy

Researched and prioritised 30+ academic institutions. Built an outreach sequence, qualification rubric and pilot-proposal templates, advancing several institutional conversations to proposal stage.

Exited when willingness to pay and procurement constraints made sustainable unit economics doubtful. That decision sharpened my focus on measurable operational value in healthcare.
